text:
Valeri Nichushkin's first season in Columbus has the shape of a role player, not the play driver Colorado leaned on. He has two goals and 10 points in 18 games, and only one goal in his last ten even as his minutes climbed to 18 a night, two more than earlier in the season.

The finishing isn't the problem. His own chances have collapsed: 0.48 expected goals per 60 this season against 1.07 last season with the Avalanche, and he is shooting 8.7%. The Blue Jackets take 51% of the shot attempts with him at five on five but slightly less than half the expected goals.

Some of that is the move. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 2.1 wins last season, a two-way driver in the 87th and 89th percentiles, but also playing with teammates in the 99th percentile. Columbus doesn't have that around him. His legs are still there (his top speed sits in the 92nd percentile by NHL Edge), and All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 55% of his entries. Watch whether the Blue Jackets give him a center who can turn those carries into looks at the net.
headline: Nichushkin's new home, quieter stick
